text:
kari: Heads up — noticed a routing oddity during today's canary. Tier:gold traffic in eu-west was sent to the preview-quant variant even though the fallback policy should have preferred stable. Anyone seen this before?

santiago: Huh. Was that for the A/B experiment or the staggered canary?

kari: Staggered exposure (per-tier). Canary config shows exposure for gold=5% -> 50% progressively. The requests that missed went to preview-quant on fallback.

maggie: Can you paste the route + fallback snippet? I want to check scope resolution.

kari: Sure — from logs & config: ```yaml
routing:
  scope: [tier:gold, region:eu-west]
  traffic_split:
    stable: 95
    preview-quant: 5
  fallback_order: [preview-quant, stable]
  fallback_policy: "prefer_low_latency"
```

zane: That fallback_order looks explicit, so preview-quant should be *first* fallback. Why would it prefer preview when it *is* the preview? Are you saying stable should be preferred but preview got chosen?

kari: Sorry, to be clearer — on overload the platform picked preview-quant as the fallback *instead of stable-legacy* which has lower latency historically. Our expectation was stable-legacy > preview-quant in fallback priority for gold.

mei: Two quick hypotheses: 1) scope overlap: if the A/B rollout is scoped at account-level while per-tier routing is tier+region, the platform may match a different variant set when evaluating fallbacks. 2) fallback_policy enum semantics — "prefer_low_latency" might reorder fallback based on observed latencies, overriding fallback_order.

maggie: Right — we recently added "fallback_policy: dynamic" to allow telemetry-driven ordering. That can supersede static fallback_order if the route-level flag `allow_dynamic_fallback=true`. Check that flag on the route.

kari: Found it — `allow_dynamic_fallback: true` was on the route. We turned it on as an experiment. That explains behavior. But two follow-ups: a) should dynamic fallback be allowed during canaries? b) console UX makes it hard to see that flag when you view per-tier rollout.

santiago: For (a) I'd say no by default. Dynamic fallback can change exposure semantics mid-rollout. We should gate it behind `dynamic_fallback_opt_in` and default to false for staged exposure.

zane: For (b) agree. The Route UI shows a single combined "Fallback" line but doesn't show whether ordering is static or telemetry-driven. We should show: enum + telemetry reason + last-eval timestamp.

maggie: Proposed API change (minimal): add `fallback_mode: "static" | "dynamic"` to the route API and console. Keep `fallback_order` for static; expose `telemetry_snapshot` for dynamic. cURL example: ```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/rt_123 \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n -d '{"fallback_mode":"static","fallback_order":["stable-legacy","preview-quant"]}'
```

mei: Back-compat notes: if `fallback_mode` is absent, use existing behavior (honor `allow_dynamic_fallback` flag). But I'd rather deprecate that flag in favour of explicit `fallback_mode`.

zane: Also need telemetry gating: if route is in canary or A/B with exposure < X% we should optionally force `fallback_mode=static` to avoid unexpected variance. Maybe default X=10%.

santiago: That needs product agreement. From an infra POV, we can add a temporary server-side override: when `rollout_type in (staged, ab)` and `exposure_pct < 10` then force static fallback ordering unless route explicitly opts in.

maggie: I'll draft console copy and API contract. If infra can add the server-side guard, we can roll quickly.

zane: Also add telemetry metric: `fallback_reorders_due_to_dynamic` with tags {route, tier, region, variant_from, variant_to}. We need to alert if >0.5% of requests change fallback order during a rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout guard feature branch deployed to staging (build #7421).

kari: Nice. Action items: Maggie -> API + console copy; Zane -> telemetry metric + infra guard; Santiago -> confirm prod-safe threshold; Mei -> update rollout docs to call out `fallback_mode` best practices. I'll own validation on the failing canary traces.

maggie: I'll open a PR for the API spec + console mockups by EOD.

zane: I'll wire telemetry and a simple alert rule; dropping here the metric name: `routing.fallback.dynamic_reorder_count`

kari: Thanks all. For now I rolled back `allow_dynamic_fallback` on the impacted route and re-ran canary. Observed stable-legacy getting the fallback path now.

mei: Good call. We'll reconvene after Maggie's PR. :thumbsup:
